title: Temporal Coalescer + KV Sparsity Controller for Mixed Prompt/Response Continuous Batching
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: We need to reduce GPU memory churn and tail latency for workloads with highly mixed prompt/response lengths by introducing a temporal coalescing heuristic in the continuous-batcher plus a KV Sparsity Controller that adaptively adjusts residency of KV shards. The goal is to improve P50/P95 latency and reduce token cost without harming quality or throughput for steady-state traffic.

Context: Current continuous-batcher shows high memory fragmentation when short prompts interleave with long generation responses; KV cache occupancy spikes lead to slab churn, OOM spikes on certain instance types, and increased preemption on Dedicated. Existing length-aware schedulers partially help but are reactive and force expensive KV evictions.

Hypothesis: By adding a small temporal coalescer that groups short prompt requests within a time window (micro-cohorts) while gating KV residency with a sparsity controller (evict low-access KV shards first and optionally compress cold shards), we can: 1) reduce the frequency of expensive KV slab rebalances, 2) keep hot context resident improving P50, and 3) avoid long tail latencies caused by reactive full-cache GC.

Design: 1) Temporal coalescer: a micro-window of 8-25ms (param) that opportunistically coalesces incoming short prompt requests into the same slot when doing so does not violate latency SLO. This differs from existing coalescers by using real-time admission scoring (latency headroom + sequence-length histogram) and backpressure signals from GPU memory allocator. 2) KV Sparsity Controller: maintains per-shard access counters and a lightweight aging score; periodically (every 250ms) computes eviction candidates and applies three tiers: hot (pin), warm (compress/quantize), cold (evict to spill). Controller exposes tunables: min-residency, compress-threshold, spill-threshold. 3) Integrations: hooks into runtime kernel selection so compressed shards use different kernels; integrates with sampler that estimates expected continuation length for active requests to avoid evicting shards likely to be used.

Metrics: P50/P95 latency for mixed workload; GPU resident KB per shard; KV eviction rate (evictions/min), number of OOMs, token cost per 1M tokens, throughput (requests/s), quality regression delta using evaluation prompts (should be <= 0.5% regression on generation perplexity/ROUGE for affected workloads).

Experiment Plan: Phase A (canary): implement coalescer + read-only sparsity scoring (no eviction) to validate scoring correlates with future access (7 days). Phase B (limited eviction on 5% of traffic, non-critical customers), measure latency/eviction trade-offs (2 weeks). Phase C (gradual rollout) with adaptive thresholds and autoscaling safety nets.

Safety & Rollback: Controller starts in conservative tuning: min-residency = 70% by default. A runtime fallback route will pin a golden model variant and reject evictions if OOM rates increase > 2x baseline. Rollback flag to disable coalescer immediately.

Acceptance Criteria: - P95 latency for mixed workloads reduced by >= 20% relative to baseline on the canary fleet without throughput loss. - KV eviction rate reduced by >= 15% (or if eviction increases, total OOMs and tail latencies must not worsen). - No quality regression > 0.5% on evaluation set. - No customer-facing errors during limited rollout.

Implementation Notes: prefer incremental PRs: runtime changes (batcher admission logic) -> telemetry (per-shard counters, histograms) -> sparsity controller service -> integration for compression kernels. Add config flags and feature gates (coalescer.enabled, kv.sparsity.mode).

Open design trade-offs: - Window size vs latency: larger windows improve coalescing but increase edge latency. We'll run param sweep 8/12/20/25ms. - Compression cost vs benefit: compressing warm shards saves memory but adds CPU overhead and kernel incompatibilities. We'll restrict compression to quantize-4 variants on GPUs with suitable kernels. - Predictive residency: using a small predictor (LR model) for continuation length could help but adds complexity — start with simple heuristic based on recent turn lengths.

Artifacts & Links: design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Temporal+Coalescer+and+KV+Sparsity+Controller (internal); Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4198 (WIP); Benchmark dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv/continuous-batcher-experiments

Next steps: merge runtime admission PR, add per-shard telemetry, run Phase A canary on 10 dedicated nodes, collect 7-day metrics, iterate thresholds.
comments: 2025-03-05 - Maya Chen: Initial ticket created after spike analysis from 2025-02-28 incident; added problem statement and hypothesis. Assigned to Liam for implementation plan.

2025-03-07 - Liam O'Connor: Pushed first draft PR with temporal coalescer admission hook (WIP). Micro-window default set to 12ms. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4198. Running local perf harness against mixlen-sim bench.
2025-03-09 - SRE review (Arjun Patel): flagged that eviction/spill path must be gated by a rate limiter to avoid sudden I/O storms. Suggested adding circuit-breaker for spill operations.
2025-03-10 - Maya Chen: Updated acceptance criteria, added initial telemetry list (per-shard access counter, eviction events, resident_kb, p50/p95 by length cohort).

2025-03-12 - Liam O'Connor: Local benchmark (A100, 80GB): with coalescer-only enabled we saw 12% P95 reduction and 8% drop in eviction rate on synthetic mixed workload (short:long ratio 70:30). Memory variance reduced by 18%. Added these results to PR description.

2025-03-14 - Design feedback (Rosa Park): propose a 'warm compression' tier using 4-bit quant for KV to avoid full evictions; requires kernel-path check. Rosa requested a follow-up RFC on kernel compatibility next week.

2025-03-14 - Liam O'Connor: Plan to enable read-only sparsity scoring in Phase A canary (no evictions) by 2025-03-17, then limited eviction in Phase B on 5% traffic by 2025-03-24. Added telemetry dashboards and alert thresholds.
